12.1.1 Meaning of the Phrase "x approaches zero"

blocks.prompt: 1 Show that the terms of \(x_{n} = \frac{1}{2n}\) approach \(0\), and find after which position every term is smaller than \(0.001\).
blocks.explanation: Terms: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{6}, \ldots\) become as small as we please as \(n\) grows, so \(x_{n} \to 0\) as \(n \to \infty\). \(\frac{1}{2n} < 0.001 \Leftrightarrow 2n > 1000 \Leftrightarrow n > 500\): every term after the 500th.

blocks.text: 12.1.2 Meaning of the Phrase "x approaches infinity"

blocks.prompt: 2 Explain why \(x_{n} = 2^{n}\) tends to infinity, and find the first \(n\) for which \(x_{n} > 1000\).
blocks.explanation: \(2, 4, 8, 16, \ldots\) increase without end and can be made as large as we please, so \(x_{n} \to \infty\) as \(n \to \infty\). \(2^{9} = 512\), \(2^{10} = 1024 > 1000\): the first such \(n\) is \(10\).

blocks.text: 12.1.5 Limit of a Function

blocks.prompt: 7 Define the limit of a function.
blocks.explanation: Let \(f(x)\) be defined in an open interval near \(a\) (need not be at \(a\)). If, as \(x\) approaches \(a\) from both the left and the right of \(a\), \(f(x)\) approaches a specific number \(L\), then \(L\) is the limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x \to a\): \(\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L\).

book_ref.quote: be defined in an open interval near the number

blocks.text: 12.1.6 Theorems on Limits of Functions

blocks.prompt: 8 State the theorem on the limit of a quotient of two functions.
blocks.explanation: If \(\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L\) and \(\lim_{x \to a} g(x) = M\), then \(\lim_{x \to a}\frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{L}{M}\), provided \(g(x) \ne 0\) in a neighbourhood of \(a\) and \(M \ne 0\).

book_ref.quote: The limit of the quotient of the functions is equal to the quotient of their limits

blocks.text: 12.3.1 One-Sided Limits

blocks.prompt: 46 Define the left hand limit and the right hand limit of \(f(x)\) at \(c\).
blocks.explanation: \(\lim_{x \to c^{-}} f(x) = L\): for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(c\) but less than \(c\), \(f(x)\) can be made as close as we please to \(L\). \(\lim_{x \to c^{+}} f(x) = M\): for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(c\) but greater than \(c\), \(f(x)\) can be made as close as we please to \(M\).

book_ref.quote: for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(c\), but less than \(c\)

blocks.text: 12.3.2 Criterion for Existence of Limit of a Function

blocks.explanation: For \(x < -2\), \(|x + 2| = -(x + 2)\), so LHL \(= -1\). For \(x > -2\), \(|x + 2| = x + 2\), so RHL \(= 1\). \(-1 \ne 1\), so the limit does not exist.

book_ref.quote: exactly when the left hand limit and the right hand limit both exist and both equal

blocks.prompt: 49 Find \(k\) so that \(\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)\) exists, where \(f(x) = kx + 1\) for \(x < 2\) and \(f(x) = x^{2} - 1\) for \(x > 2\).
blocks.explanation: LHL \(= 2k + 1\), RHL \(= 4 - 1 = 3\). The limit exists when \(2k + 1 = 3\), i.e. \(k = 1\).

book_ref.quote: Method: \(x = 2\) and \(x = 4\) are the points where the formula changes

blocks.text: 12.3.3 Continuity of a Function at a Point

blocks.prompt: 50 When is a function \(f\) said to be continuous at \(x = c\)?
blocks.explanation: \(f\) is continuous at \(c\) if and only if (i) \(f(c)\) is defined, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x)\) exists, (iii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)\). If any one fails, \(f\) is discontinuous at \(c\).

book_ref.quote: if and only if the following three conditions are satisfied

blocks.prompt: 51 Is \(f(x) = \frac{x^{2} - 25}{x - 5}\) continuous at \(x = 5\)? Give a reason.
blocks.explanation: No. \(f(5) = \frac{0}{0}\) is not defined, so condition (i) fails and \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = 5\) (though \(\lim_{x \to 5} f(x) = 10\)).

book_ref.quote: If one or more of these three conditions fail to hold

blocks.prompt: 55 An investment grows as \(A(t) = 2000e^{0.08t}\) (rupees). Find \(A(25)\) and the limit as \(t \to \infty\).
blocks.explanation: \(A(25) = 2000e^{2} \approx 14778.11\) rupees. Since \(0.08t \to \infty\), \(e^{0.08t} \to \infty\), so \(\lim_{t \to \infty} A(t) = \infty\): the value grows without bound.

book_ref.quote: The value of an investment grows according to the formula for continuous compounding

blocks.prompt: 56 The demand function is \(D(p) = \frac{500}{2p + 5}\). Find \(\lim_{p \to \infty} D(p)\) and interpret it.
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{500/p}{2 + 5/p} \to \frac{0}{2} = 0\). As the price becomes very large, the demand approaches \(0\).

book_ref.quote: the demand function \(D(p)\) decreases as the price \(p\) increases
